text:
IncidentBot: :rotating_light: ALERT: kv-cache size runaway + cont-batch perf cliff detected across llama/mistral combo. Paging SRE oncall. Root cause unknown, suspected prefetch/continuous-batching interaction.

maya: seeing sustained 3x P95 for llama-* routes since 09:07 UTC. KV cache growing on shard-11/12, eviction not keeping up. Some requests getting 503s when shard memory crosses threshold. Customers A and B reporting timeouts.

trevor: noted a sudden jump in continuous-batch sizes around 09:06 — distribution shows many batches with 10-12 requests instead of usual 2-3 for short prompts. likely prefix-KV cache misses + long-lived conversations.

eli: logs show lots of `kv_put` churn and prefix cache keys not being reused. stack traces point at `cont_batch_assembler` holding onto requests while waiting for open slots.

maya: quick telemetry:
```
kv_cache_size_mb: shard-11=18GB -> 42GB in 6m
cont_batch_avg_size: 2.1 -> 9.7
p95_latency_ms: model=llama-v2-13b: 120ms -> 380ms
errors_503_rate: 0.2% -> 3.4%
```

sanjay: paging and triage: I'm on it. priority: mitigate customer impact, then root cause. assigning to @trevor + @eli for hotfix. @zoe-cs please prepare customer comms.

zoe-cs: pinged Customer A with "we're investigating increased latency and intermittent errors, will post an update in 30m". Customer B on standby.

trevor: proposal for immediate live mitigation (low-risk):
- disable continuous-batching for llama models (toggle per-model flag)
- reduce `cont_batch_max_wait_ms` from 50 -> 10 for other models temporarily
- increase kv eviction aggressiveness TTL from 15m -> 1m on affected shards

eli: agree. fast commands:
```
# disable cont-batch for llama routes (canary to two nodes first)
rdr config set --model-prefix llama- --key cont_batch_enabled=false --scope runtime --canary 2
# quick eviction bump
rdr runtime patch-shard --shard shard-11 --kv-eviction-ttl 60
```

maya: can we do the canary to two nodes and watch before global? we saw earlier hotfixes cause small regressions.

trevor: will do canary. will also add a routing fallback rule to route new llama requests to mistral-qwen-compat if latency doesn't recover in 5m. fallback only for non-auth customers.

eli: kicking off canary now. logs: `deploy/feature-toggle` event at 09:12.

IncidentBot: :gear: Feature toggle rollout event: cont_batch_enabled=false for prefix=llama- (canary nodes: r-22, r-23).

maya: after canary at 09:15: shard-11 eviction reduced memory trend, p95 for canary nodes dropped ~45%. global rollback window 09:20.

trevor: still seeing elevated batches on non-canary nodes; proceeding to roll out to all nodes at 09:18 with staged 20% increments. monitor dashboards.

eli: applied eviction TTL bump on shard-11/12 and shard-14. memory slope flattened.

zoe-cs: updating Customer A: "We've applied a temporary routing/hotfix to reduce latency; you may still see intermittent 503s for a short window while we finish rollout."

maya: post-rollout check at 09:25: global p95 back to ~140ms for llama routes, errors down to 0.4%. cont-batch avg size back to ~3. Good so far.

trevor: follow-ups (action items):
- create small regression test reproducing cont-batch + prefix-kv workload for llama/mistral combos (owner: trevor)
- instrument batch assembler to expose hold-time histograms (owner: eli)
- add a runtime-safe guard: if kv_cache_growth_rate > X then auto-disable cont-batch for that model prefix (owner: runtime team)

eli: quick note on root cause theory: some conversation workloads generate many ephemeral prefix tokens (high diversity) so kv hits are low, causing cont-batcher to aggregate more requests trying to amortize GPU ops — this increases memory pressure on KV caches and leads to eviction thrashing. combination with recent change in prefetch heuristics likely amplified it.

maya: tagging for postmortem: severity=sev2, customer-impacting. we'll schedule follow-up meeting.

zoe-cs: CS notes: Customer A observed 12 failed requests and 40 slow responses during the window (09:06-09:26). Customer B 5 failures. both ok with incident updates.

sanjay: handing off to oncall followup rotation. leaving oncall channel at 09:30. please draft brief for PMs and support.

IncidentBot: :white_check_mark: Incident mitigated — monitoring. Create postmortem when stable.

maya: final: we'll include metrics, config diffs, and the reproduction harness in the postmortem. thanks all for quick action. :heart:
